message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it might be a STEMI, right?
reply:
**I wouldn’t call this a definite STEMI from this image, but it cannot exclude an acute heart attack.**

My reading is:

- Sinus rhythm, approximately **65 beats/minute**.
- Very high QRS voltage, with deep anterior S waves and tall lateral R waves—suggesting **left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH)**.
- Prominent anterior T waves and some ST changes, without a clear diagnostic pattern of ST elevation in neighboring leads.

LVH can produce ST/T changes that resemble ischemia; the distinction requires symptoms, comparison with previous ECGs, and repeat tracings. [ACC/AHA guideline](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009)

**If there is current or recent chest pain, breathlessness, sweating, or faintness, seek emergency assessment now and don’t drive yourself.** Repeat ECGs and troponin testing are needed; an ECG without clear STEMI does not rule out a heart attack. [American Heart Association](https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/heart-attack/warning-signs-of-a-heart-attack)
